messages:
marta: heads-up — ECC corrected errors spiking on eu-west-1-gpu-pool-2 over the last 10m. Seeing repeat Xid 13 on host gpu-node-12 and rising corrected counts on gpu-node-7.

marta: quick snapshot from prometheus: `gpu_ecc_corrected_total{node="gpu-node-12"} +27 in 600s`

marta: stacktrace-ish from syslog: ```nvidia: ECC error corrected on GPU 3 (Xid 13) -- GPC TPC ecc syndrome 0x4f```

sanjay: ack. are those nodes already marked draining?

marta: not yet. no automated drains triggered. alerting rule fired but the auto-drain policy thresholds look conservative and didn't flip.

liam: what's current policy? I thought auto-drain triggers at 50 corrected ECC in 1h or 10 Xid errors in 10m.

marta: current rule (ops-alerts/gpu-ecc): `corrected_ecc > 50 over 3600s` OR `xid_errors > 10 over 600s`. This spike hits the second condition only if we aggregate differently; per-GPU the numbers are lower so the rule didn't escalate to auto-drain.

anya: from past incidents, small but repeated Xid 13 on a single GPU is usually prologue to flakiness. We should probably have a per-card short-window threshold that recommends quarantine.

liam: propose: new soft-threshold: if any single GPU reports >=5 corrected ECC or >=3 Xid 13 events within 10m, set node to QUARANTINE (taint but don't immediate-evict), notify oncall. Hard-threshold: >=10 corrected ECC or >=6 Xid in 10m -> auto-drain + replace.

sanjay: +1 on separating soft/hard. But need ramp control per-pool to avoid mass drains in low-capacity pods (eu-west-1 has tight capacity). Add a cooldown window and max-simultaneous-drains per pool.

marta: agreed. suggested pool config: `max_simultaneous_drains=1`, `cooldown=30m` for eu-west-1-gpu-pool-2. Other pools can be 2 or 3 depending on spare capacity.

liam: ops-bot, can you show recent drain history for that pool?

ops-bot: pull complete. Recent drains for eu-west-1-gpu-pool-2: [2026-01-14 gpu-node-3], [2026-02-20 gpu-node-8]. Only 2 drains in last 90 days. Current running allocs: 78% capacity.

anya: so capacity is tight — auto-drain hard threshold should fallback to canary replacement (mark node for dev-only evictions) if pool utilization > 85%?

liam: alternative: prefer live-card blacklisting (kernel-level isolate) if supported, instead of full node drain, to avoid evicting pods. Kernel hot-unplug isn't great for our drivers though. We should document that option but not default it.

sanjay: operational checklist draft: 1) run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and capture ECC counts 2) check dmesg for Xid entries 3) kubectl cordon + annotate `redwood/quarantine-reason=ecc-spike` 4) if hard-threshold -> `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and trigger replacement playbook.

marta: include exact commands in runbook: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl annotate node gpu-node-12 redwood/quarantine-reason=ecc-spike``` and for drain: ```kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --force --delete-local-data```

liam: add a safety check: ensure autoscaler or capacity pool has spare nodes before drain. If not, switch to `quarantine` label + manual followup ticket to infra-team for RMA.

ops-bot: noted. I'll create an automation PR template that: 1) evaluates per-GPU short-window metrics, 2) applies soft/quarantine taint, 3) re-checks after 10m, 4) escalates to hard-drain if persistent and pool has spare capacity.

anya: for alerting message content — include per-GPU counts, node ID, recent dmesg snippet, and current pool utilization. Keep it actionable.

marta: also add a regression guard: if automation triggers >2 drains in 1h in any pool, auto-disable and notify #eng-oncall and #eng-sre.

liam: agree. And create a small eval job to run on sample of past incidents to validate thresholds (false positives vs missed failures).

sanjay: can someone open the ticket for runbook + automation PR? I'll pick up the RMA docs.

marta: I'll open the ticket and add the checklist, then add an RFC link. https://redwood.example.com/issue/RI-3421

liam: ping @oncall-team when PR is ready. We'll put a feature flag for 2 weeks behind a kill-switch.

marta: thanks. action items: (1) marta: create ticket + runbook update (RI-3421) (2) ops-bot: draft automation PR template (3) liam & anya: run eval on historical incidents (4) sanjay: RMA + hardware tracking doc.

marta: for now I've cordoned gpu-node-12 and annotated it as quarantine. Monitoring will keep an eye.

sanjay: thx, will follow up. :thumbsup:
